name: AI and LLM features

name: AI chat interface

name: Streaming LLM responses

name: Text embeddings

triggers: use a cheaper model for easy questions;which ai model should i use;send hard questions to a smarter model;mix cheap and expensive models;faster model for simple tasks;switch models per task
requirements: Define the task types and test each candidate model on them with evals before choosing;Route on clear signals such as a classifier, task type or input size, not guesswork;Escalate to a larger model when the small one fails validation or reports low confidence;Compare total cost including retries and escalations, not just price per token;Log which model handled each request so quality can be compared;Re-test routing rules when models or prices change
done_when: Eval scores per route meet the quality bar;Most simple requests are served by the cheaper model;The model used is recorded for every request

name: LLM outage and overload fallback
explanation: Coping when the AI provider is down, overloaded or rate-limiting, by retrying sensibly, switching to a backup model and telling the user clearly what happened.
synonyms: llm failover;model fallback;provider failover;ai outage handling;overloaded error
triggers: ai service is down;chatbot stopped working;too many requests from openai;ai model overloaded;backup ai provider;ai request timed out
requirements: Retry rate-limit, overloaded and server errors with exponential backoff and jitter, and respect any retry-after header;Do not retry invalid request or authentication errors;Set a timeout and cap total retries so users are not left waiting;Fall back to another model or provider that has been tested with the same prompts;Show a clear message and keep the user's input when no model is available;Alert when error or fallback rates rise
done_when: A simulated overload triggers retries then the fallback model;Users see a helpful message instead of a blank or a hang;The user's text is not lost after a failure

name: Model version pinning and upgrades
explanation: Using an exact, dated model version in production, watching for its retirement date and testing a new version with evals before switching.
synonyms: model pinning;model snapshot;model deprecation;model retirement;model migration
triggers: ai answers changed suddenly;model is being retired;upgrade to a newer ai model;lock the ai model version;model end of life date;switch to the latest model
requirements: Use a specific dated model id in production instead of an alias that moves to new versions;Keep the model id in configuration, not scattered in code;Track the provider's deprecation and retirement dates and set reminders well ahead;Run your evals on the new model and adjust prompts before switching;Roll out the new model gradually and keep a way to switch back until it is retired;Record which model version produced each stored output
done_when: Production uses an exact model id from configuration;Evals pass on the new model before the switch;Each logged response shows its model version

name: LLM tracing and observability
explanation: Recording every AI model and tool call with its prompt version, token use, latency, cost and errors, so you can debug answers and watch quality and spend.
synonyms: llm tracing;genai telemetry;llm monitoring;ai call logging;ai observability
triggers: why did the ai say that;see what prompt was sent;track ai token usage;ai cost per user;debug ai answers;monitor the chatbot
requirements: Create a span for each model call, tool call and retrieval step under one trace per user request;Record model name, prompt version, input and output tokens, latency, finish reason and errors;Follow the OpenTelemetry gen_ai semantic conventions so tools can read the data;Make capture of full prompts and responses opt-in and redact personal data;Compute cost per request from token counts and alert on spikes;Link traces to user feedback and eval results
done_when: Any answer can be traced to its exact prompt, model and tool calls;Token use and cost are visible per feature;No raw personal data appears in traces by default

name: AI disclosure and content labelling
explanation: Making it clear to people when they are talking to an AI and visibly marking text, images, audio or video that an AI produced.
synonyms: ai disclosure;ai label;ai-generated label;eu ai act transparency;synthetic content labelling
triggers: tell users it is a bot;label ai generated images;made with ai badge;mark ai written text;is this a real person;deepfake label
requirements: Tell people they are interacting with an AI at the start, unless it is obvious from context;Label AI-generated or edited images, audio and video where people see them, not only in settings;Add machine-readable marking to generated media as well as the visible label;Keep labels when content is shared, downloaded or embedded;Make labels readable by screen readers and in all themes;Do not present AI output as written or spoken by a real person
done_when: Users can tell from the first screen that they are talking to an AI;Every generated image or clip shows a label;Downloaded media still carries the marking

name: Content provenance (C2PA)
explanation: Attaching signed, tamper-evident information to images, video or audio, such as C2PA Content Credentials, that records how it was made, including whether AI generated it.
synonyms: c2pa;content credentials;content provenance;media provenance manifest;provenance metadata
triggers: prove an image is ai generated;check where an image came from;sign generated images;tamper proof image history;content credentials badge
requirements: Embed a C2PA manifest that states the content was AI generated and by which tool;Sign the manifest with a certificate kept in secure key storage;Keep or update the manifest when images are resized, converted or edited in your pipeline;Use an invisible watermark too, since metadata is easily stripped;Validate manifests on upload and show the result to users;Do not put personal data in the manifest unless the user agrees
done_when: A public C2PA verify tool reads and validates the manifest on exported files;Edited files keep a valid provenance chain;Tampering makes validation fail

name: Human review of AI output
explanation: Sending AI results that are uncertain or high-stakes to a person who approves, edits or rejects them before they take effect.
synonyms: human in the loop;human-in-the-loop review;ai approval step;human oversight;ai output review queue
triggers: someone checks the ai first;approve before ai sends;review ai decisions;ai drafts and a person approves;flag unsure ai answers;manual check of ai results
requirements: Define which outputs need review, such as low confidence, high impact or irreversible actions;Show the reviewer the input, the AI output and its sources so they can judge quickly;Let reviewers approve, edit or reject and record who decided and why;Block the action until a decision is made and set a time limit with a safe default;Watch for rubber-stamping by sampling approved items and tracking approval rates;Feed reviewer edits back into evals and prompt improvements
done_when: No high-stakes AI action runs without a recorded human decision;Each decision shows reviewer, time and reason;Reviewer corrections appear in the eval set

name: Feedback on AI responses
explanation: Letting users rate or report AI answers, for example thumbs up or down with a reason or a correction, and using that feedback to improve the system.
synonyms: thumbs up thumbs down;response rating;ai answer feedback;response feedback widget;user feedback loop
triggers: was this answer helpful;rate the ai answer;report a wrong ai answer;thumbs down on chatbot reply;let users correct the ai
requirements: Put rating controls on each response, labelled and usable by keyboard and screen reader;Ask an optional reason after a thumbs down, such as wrong, unsafe or not helpful;Save the feedback with the trace id, prompt version and model;Tell users what happens with feedback and whether conversations are reviewed;Let users report harmful output separately from general rating;Review negative feedback regularly and add real failures to eval sets
done_when: Each rating is linked to the exact response and trace;Harmful-content reports reach a review queue;Negative examples are added to the eval set

name: Explaining AI results and confidence
explanation: Showing users why the AI gave a result and how sure it is, so they know when to rely on it and when to check it themselves.
synonyms: ai explainability;confidence score;uncertainty display;why this result;model confidence indicator
triggers: why did the ai suggest this;how sure is the ai;show ai confidence;ai might be wrong warning;explain the recommendation
requirements: Explain results in terms users understand, such as the inputs or sources that mattered most;Show confidence only if it is calibrated and tested, otherwise use plain categories or none;Say clearly when the AI is unsure and suggest how to check;Do not imply more certainty or human-like reasoning than the system has;Keep explanations short with an option to see more detail;Test with users that explanations change how much they trust results appropriately
done_when: Low-confidence results are visibly marked;Users can see what a result was based on;Shown confidence matches measured accuracy

name: Setting expectations for AI features
explanation: Explaining up front what an AI feature can and cannot do, how well it does it and how to use it, with example prompts and known limits.
synonyms: ai onboarding;ai capability disclosure;ai limitations notice;example prompts
triggers: explain what the ai can do;ai can make mistakes notice;example questions to ask the ai;first time using the ai;what the assistant cannot do
requirements: Say what the feature does and the main things it cannot do in plain words;Warn that it can make mistakes and say what users should check;Offer a few example prompts that actually work well;Explain what data it uses and whether it learns from the user;Show the information again where users need it, not only once at sign up;Update the guidance when the model or feature changes
done_when: New users can say what the feature is for after onboarding;Example prompts give good results;A limits note is visible near the AI input

name: Inline AI writing suggestions
explanation: AI completions or rewrites shown inside a text editor that the user can preview and then accept, edit or dismiss without losing what they wrote.
synonyms: ghost text;ai autocomplete;inline completion;ai rewrite;ai text completion
triggers: suggest the next words;ai help me write;rewrite this paragraph;accept suggestion with tab;improve my writing with ai;ai completes my sentence
requirements: Show suggestions so they are clearly distinct from the user's own text;Accept with one key or click, and dismiss easily by continuing to type or pressing Escape;Never overwrite the user's text without preview and make accepts undoable;Cancel pending requests when the user keeps typing and drop stale suggestions;Make suggestions available to screen readers and do not steal focus;Let users turn suggestions off or tone them down
done_when: Typing over a suggestion keeps the user's text intact;Undo restores the text from before an accepted rewrite;Suggestions can be fully turned off

name: AI summarization
explanation: Using AI to write a short version of a long document, meeting or thread that keeps to what the source says, at a set length and format.
synonyms: summarization;text summarization;ai summary;tldr generation;meeting summary
triggers: summarize this document;give me the key points;shorten a long email thread;meeting notes from transcript;summary of a long report;one paragraph overview
requirements: Define the audience, length and format, such as bullet points or set sections;Tell the model to use only the source and say when information is missing;Split documents longer than the context into parts and combine part summaries;Link key points back to the place in the source where possible;Check faithfulness with evals that catch added or wrong facts;Mark summaries as AI generated and link to the full source
done_when: Summaries contain no facts that are not in the source;Long documents are summarized without context errors;Length and format match the spec

name: LLM text classification
explanation: Using an AI model to sort text into a fixed set of categories, such as routing support tickets or detecting intent, tested against labelled examples.

triggers: sort tickets by topic;detect what the user wants;tag messages automatically;route emails to the right team;categorize feedback with ai;spam or not spam
requirements: Define each category with a clear description and a few examples in the prompt;Include an other or unsure category for text that fits none;Force output to one of the allowed labels with structured output and reject anything else;Build a labelled test set from real data and measure accuracy per category;Send low-confidence or unknown results to a fallback such as a person;Re-run the test set when categories, prompt or model change

name: Image and document input to LLMs
explanation: Sending images, screenshots, scans or PDFs to an AI model that can read them, so it can describe them, extract details or answer questions about them.
synonyms: multimodal input;vision model;image understanding;pdf input to llm;document understanding
triggers: ask ai about a photo;read text from a screenshot;ai reads my pdf;extract data from a receipt image;describe this picture;chat with a pdf
requirements: Check the provider's supported formats and limits on file size, pixel size, page count and number of images;Resize large images before sending to save tokens and stay within limits;Count image and PDF pages toward the token budget;Treat text inside images and documents as untrusted, since it can carry prompt injection;Validate uploads and strip metadata that should not be shared;Tell users the model can misread small text, charts or handwriting and verify key values

name: AI image generation
explanation: Letting users create or edit images from a text description, with choices of size and quality, safety checks and storage of the results.
synonyms: text to image;image generation;ai art;image editing with ai;generative images
triggers: make a picture from text;ai generated images;create a logo with ai;edit a photo with a prompt;generate product images
requirements: Check prompts and generated images against your content policy and handle refusals clearly;Offer only the sizes and quality levels the model supports and show cost or wait time;Show progress, since generation can take many seconds;Store generated images yourself, since returned data or links may not be kept;Label images as AI generated and keep provenance metadata;Limit how many images each user can generate

name: AI text-to-speech
explanation: Turning text, often written by an AI, into natural-sounding speech with a chosen voice, playing it as it streams and making clear the voice is AI.

triggers: read the answer aloud;ai voice for my app;turn text into audio;natural sounding voice;ai narration
requirements: Tell listeners that the voice is AI generated, as provider policies require;Stream audio so playback starts before the whole text is processed;Pick an output format that suits playback, such as a compressed format for web and raw PCM for low latency;Split long text at sentence boundaries to stay under the input limit;Give users play, pause and speed controls and show the text too;Do not clone or imitate a real person's voice without consent

name: AI speech transcription
explanation: Turning recorded or live speech into text with an AI speech model, handling languages, timestamps, long recordings and unclear words.
synonyms: ai transcription;transcription api;automatic speech recognition;asr;audio transcription
triggers: transcribe a recording;turn audio into text;transcribe meeting audio;subtitles from audio;voice notes to text;who said what in a recording
requirements: Check supported audio formats and the upload size limit and split long files at pauses, not mid-word;Set the language when known instead of relying on detection;Give the model a prompt or vocabulary for names and terms it may misspell;Request timestamps when text must line up with audio, such as for captions;Turn on speaker labels (diarization) when you need who said what and check the model supports it;Show uncertain or unclear passages and let users edit the transcript;Get consent before recording and protect audio as personal data

name: Real-time voice assistant
explanation: A spoken conversation with an AI where audio streams both ways with low delay, the AI knows when the user has finished speaking and can be interrupted.

requirements: Use WebRTC in browsers and apps and WebSocket for server to server audio;Mint short-lived client tokens on your server and never ship the main API key;Use voice activity detection to detect end of turn and tune it for noise;Stop playback at once when the user speaks and truncate the unheard reply from history;Show a live transcript and a clear listening or speaking state;Tell users they are speaking with an AI and handle dropped connections
